item.title: Phone-Free Policies Improve Focus, Safety, and Academic Success
item.dc:creator: Guest User
item.description: Phone Ban vs. Phone-Free: What’s the difference? Not all school phone policies are effective; some are too vague or difficult to enforce, making a clear, consistent policy—and program—essential.
item.content:encoded:
Cell phones and social media are increasingly disrupting student focus, performance, and mental health. In response, the U.S. Department of Education is urging the adoption of clear, research-based policies for cell phone use in schools, emphasizing the importance of creating policies that meet the unique needs of each school community. A growing number of states have implemented legislation or unlocked funding to restrict the use of cell phones and wearable tech in schools. In addition, districts and schools have implemented their own phone-use restrictions.

However, not all phone policies are effective; some are too vague or difficult to enforce, making a clear, consistent policy—and program—essential. 

“Cellphone bans are in place in 77% of schools. But this high number seems to refer to... any school that tells students they should not use their phone while in class. That's not really a ban; it's more of an unenforceable wish.”

- Jonathan Haidt, Author and Social Psychologist,
The Atlantic: Get Phones Out of Schools Now

Yondr’s All-Day Solution

More than just a pouch, The Yondr Phone-Free Schools Program is a complete bell-to-bell solution combining patented technology, tailored training, and ongoing support.

  • Phone-Free Equipment: Essential tools like pouches, unlocking bases, and lockboxes make the transition to a phone-free environment seamless.

  • Training & Support: Year-round program support, including pre-launch planning, mid-year check-ins, and end-of-year reviews, ensures success every step of the way.

  • Curriculum Resources: Customizable presentations, lesson plans, and activity guides help educators and parents build healthy digital habits beyond the classroom.

 Yondr schools report dramatic improvements in academic performance, classroom engagement, and social connection, alongside a significant decrease in cyberbullying and behavioral incidents. Many teachers at Yondr schools have reported gaining as much as 10 minutes of additional teaching and learning time each lesson. In addition to reported benefits in learning and behavioral outcomes for students, Yondr schools have reported improved work environments for staff.

Yondr’s patented lockable pouch allows students to maintain ownership of their devices while reinforcing boundaries for a focused and supportive learning environment. While phone bans and cell phone collection methods are often equated with punishment or being in trouble, Yondr’s all-day solution makes a positive difference for students in a much less confrontational way. With Yondr, students are not tempted to break policy, lose focus, and potentially suffer school consequences. They don’t worry about missing out on the digital world because their classmates’ phones are out of sight and out of mind, too. Instead, they get a much needed 6-8 hour break from digital distractions.  

“I have had teachers come in my office from other states, numerous hires and from other schools… they say they won’t go to a school without the [Yondr] cell phone pouch. Teachers are looking for help with distractions like this because it interrupts their lessons.”

- Ewell Fuller, Principal, Stanhope Elmore High School
The Wetumpka Herald: Cell Phone Policy Leads to School of Distinction

At Yondr, our mission is to create spaces where students can BE HERE NOW. Let’s work together to create a phone-free space where students can disconnect from their phones and truly connect with each other.

item.title: Blog Post Title Two
item.dc:creator: Guest User
item.description: It all begins with an idea.
item.content:encoded:
It all begins with an idea. Maybe you want to launch a business. Maybe you want to turn a hobby into something more. Or maybe you have a creative project to share with the world. Whatever it is, the way you tell your story online can make all the difference.

Don’t worry about sounding professional. Sound like you. There are over 1.5 billion websites out there, but your story is what’s going to separate this one from the rest. If you read the words back and don’t hear your own voice in your head, that’s a good sign you still have more work to do.

Be clear, be confident and don’t overthink it. The beauty of your story is that it’s going to continue to evolve and your site can evolve with it. Your goal should be to make it feel right for right now. Later will take care of itself. It always does.
